what.text: Saw palmetto is an extract of the fruit (berries) of the Serenoa repens palm. Lab studies suggest it may reduce the action of male hormones such as testosterone and may reduce inflammation; how it acts is not fully known.

src.label: EMA, saw palmetto fruit herbal medicine summary

what.text: In the US it is sold as a dietary supplement: herbs and other botanicals are dietary ingredients under the law that defines dietary supplements.

src.label: 21 U.S.C. 321(ff), definition of dietary supplement, govinfo

what.text: There is little research on saw palmetto for hair loss. Large trials for prostate symptoms found no benefit.

research.text: The hair-loss evidence is a handful of small or open-label studies, often of mixed products. NIH says the evidence is too limited to reach conclusions. For an enlarged prostate, two large US trials found saw palmetto no better than placebo.

research.title: Saw palmetto vs finasteride (Rossi et al.)

facts.v: 100 men with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia
saw palmetto 320 mg a day or finasteride 1 mg a day
photo-based score at the start and end

research.found: 38% of men on saw palmetto had more hair growth vs 68% on finasteride.

src.label: Rossi et al., Int J Immunopathol Pharmacol

research.title: A proprietary saw palmetto extract (Ablon)

facts.v: 60 healthy adult men and women with self-perceived thinning hair (40 active, 20 placebo)
terminal and vellus hair counts, hair density

research.found: Terminal hair count rose by 18.6 on the extract vs a fall of 10.1 on placebo. No treatment-related adverse events. The extract is a branded ingredient named in the paper.

research.text: A 2020 systematic review found 5 randomized trials and 2 cohort studies of products containing saw palmetto, many combined with other ingredients. It said high-quality data are lacking and larger trials of saw palmetto alone are needed.

src.label: Evron et al., Skin Appendage Disord (systematic review)

research.text: In a 2018 study, a saw palmetto extract improved survival of skin cells exposed to DHT, and in mice given DHT to cause hair loss it increased hair density, weight and thickness. These are cell and animal results only.

src.label: Eur Rev Med Pharmacol Sci, saw palmetto in hair-loss mice

research.title: STEP (Bent et al.)

facts.v: 225 men over 49 with moderate to severe BPH symptoms
saw palmetto extract 160 mg twice a day or placebo
urinary symptom score (AUASI), urine flow, prostate size, PSA

research.found: No difference from placebo on symptoms, urine flow, prostate size, quality of life or PSA. Side effects were similar.

src.label: Bent et al., N Engl J Med (STEP)

research.title: CAMUS (Barry et al.)

facts.v: double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial at 11 sites
369 men aged 45 and older with urinary symptoms
saw palmetto extract, rising from 320 mg to 960 mg a day, or placebo

research.found: Symptom scores fell by 2.20 points on saw palmetto and 2.99 on placebo. Saw palmetto was no better than placebo on any measure. No clearly attributable side effects.

us.text: Saw palmetto is not an FDA-approved drug for hair loss or any other use. It is sold as a dietary supplement. FDA does not have the authority to approve dietary supplements before they are marketed. As of November 1, 2026.

side.text: Saw palmetto is usually well tolerated in studies. Side effects are mild and uncommon. FDA does not review supplements for safety before they are sold.

items.text: NCCIH lists digestive symptoms, dizziness and headache. EMA lists stomach pain and headache in 1 to 10 in 100 people.

unconfirmed: Saw palmetto's status in Canada (natural health products), the UK and Australia was not checked against a regulator record.
The 2023 oral and topical saw palmetto oil trial and a 2025 study of a mixed supplement were found in PubMed but not reviewed.
surprises: In the only head-to-head study with finasteride found (open-label, 100 men, 2 years), 38% improved on saw palmetto vs 68% on finasteride.
Two large US trials (STEP, 225 men; CAMUS, 369 men up to triple dose) found saw palmetto no better than placebo for prostate symptoms, while the EU herbal monograph still lists it for BPH symptoms.
